summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and multiple biliary drains, was admitted with a low-grade fever and abnormal green-yellow discharge from his PTBD and percutaneous cholecystostomy tubes. He reported tenderness at the drain sites and mild nausea but denied vomiting or abdominal pain. Initial labs showed no leukocytosis or liver enzyme elevation, and blood cultures remained negative. He was started on IV meropenem for possible biliary infection but was afebrile upon admission. Interventional radiology performed a successful exchange of both the PTBD and cholecystostomy tubes, revealing a blocked PTBD that was cleared with balloon sweeping. Post-procedure, he remained stable, afebrile, and asymptomatic. A staging CT scan showed no progression of cholangiocarcinoma, stable biliary dilation, and no new metastatic lesions. Antibiotics were discontinued, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor for fever, pain, or drain changes, and to follow up on rising alkaline phosphatase levels.
